result.summary: The fragmentary hymn lists rival claims for Dionysus' birthplace, rejects them, and says Zeus bore him secretly far from Hera. Zeus then promises honours with a nod that shakes Olympus, and the poet closes with a farewell to Dionysus and Semele.

scenes.title: Disputed birthplaces of Dionysus
scenes.summary: The poet lists places claimed as Dionysus' birthplace, calls them false, and says Zeus gave him birth in secret from Hera.

scenes.title: Zeus promises honours with a nod
scenes.summary: Zeus promises that mortals will honour with offerings and sacrifice every third year, and he confirms it with a nod that shakes Olympus.

scenes.title: Closing invocation and farewell
scenes.summary: The singer asks Dionysus' favour and bids farewell to him and Semele.

alias_notes.explanation: Name by which men call Semele, who is later deified as Thyone.
Epithet referring to his birth, sewn into Zeus' thigh.

notable_quotes.reason: The poet dismisses all rival birthplace claims as lies.

analysis.text: The hymn deals with Dionysus' uncertain origins and confirms his divine legitimacy through Zeus' nod.
The competing birthplaces reflect rival local cults, and the triennial feasts reflect real festivals of Dionysus.

fun_facts.text: The hymn survives only as a fragment, with the opening lost and gaps marked by asterisks.

language_notes.text: "Insewn" refers to the myth that Zeus sewed the unborn Dionysus into his thigh; the title is an epithet of the god.
Nysa is the legendary mountain where Dionysus was nursed; ancient writers placed it in many different lands.
"Hecatombs" were large sacrifices, originally of a hundred oxen; "perfect" means unblemished and complete.
"Each three years" means every third year, by Greek inclusive counting, a festival held in alternate years.
Thyone is another name for Semele, who was said to be raised to divinity after her death.

context_notes.text: Semele was a Theban princess, mother of Dionysus by Zeus. Dracanum, Icarus, Naxos and the Alpheus were rival claimants to his birth.
Hera, Zeus' wife, was jealous of his mortal lovers and hostile to Semele and Dionysus, so the birth was concealed.
Zeus is called Son of Cronos, a title recalling his father, the Titan Cronos, whom he overthrew.

literary_notes.text: The poet bluntly dismisses rival traditions as lies, taking a confident authoritative narrator's stance.
Zeus' nod makes a whole mountain shake, conveying his overwhelming power and the binding force of his promise.
The singer addresses the god directly, asking his favour and shifting from narrative to prayer.
